 Video: ICE vehicle appears to strike pedestrian, Woodland police investigating

 A screenshot from a video posted on NorCal Resist’s social media pages from a reported ICE incident with a pedestrian on Tuesday, Oct. 20. COURTESY 
 By Taylor Heeden | theeden@dailydemocrat.com PUBLISHED: October 20, 2026 at 3:02 PM PDT | UPDATED: October 20, 2026 at 9:51 PM PDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 The public is demanding answers after federal agents appeared to be involved in an apparent hit-and-run accident with a pedestrian, launching an investigation by the Woodland Police Department.
 According to the WPD, the incident happened at 9:38 a.m. near Locust Street and Clover Street in a residential area.
 A video posted on NorCal Resist’s Facebook page shows an unmarked car, now confirmed by local law enforcement to be federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers, attempting to leave an area by Locust and Clover streets. As the Tahoe makes its escape, the vehicle swerves and looks to have struck a pedestrian, causing them to flip over the front, passenger side of the car.
 WPD responded and is now investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
 “Woodland PD responded, contacted the involved parties, and is actively investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident,” a post from the department’s Facebook reads. “We understand the community’s interest and will provide additional information as appropriate.”
 Woodland’s U.S. Congressional Rep. Mike Thompson also released a statement following the accident, calling for immediate accountability and transparency.
 “ICE cannot continue to terrorize our communities,” Thompson stated. “No one is above the law. ICE’s actions have contributed to growing distrust and fear within our communities, making transparency and accountability all the more critical. Members of our community need to feel safe.”
 This comes following reports of a 45-day-long federal immigration enforcement operation called “Operation Safe California,” which is targeting the Central Valley and southern California. The operation began in early October, around Oct. 4, according to NBC 7 San Diego, and is scheduled to run for approximately 45 days through mid-November.
 This is an ongoing investigation. The Daily Democrat will update as appropriate.
